# Component provenance

AOSP Car Dialer is adapted from Google's official prebuilt, pinned by repository revision and APK hash in dependency-revisions.json. Its upstream README identifies the app source as the June 23, 2022 AOSP release. `scripts/build_car_dialer.py` retains its resources, bundled notices and application code except for the documented non-Automotive service adapters and compact-layout selection. It replaces the packaged `CarUxRestrictions` SDK stub with the actual Apache-2.0 AOSP source pinned alongside the APK. The AOSP Apache license is preserved in licenses/AOSP-APACHE-2.0; preserve the upstream source copyright notices as well. No Automotive framework JAR is transplanted into Android. Review all bundled dependency notices before distributing the resulting APK.

Bluetooth voice uses BlueZ sbc 2.1 (LGPL-2.1-or-later) for mSBC. Its official source archive and SHA-256 are pinned in dependency-revisions.json; COPYING.LIB is preserved in licenses/. Set SBC_SOURCE to the extracted upstream directory when building. Keep that exact source and this project's adapter/build scripts available with any distributed calling binary; the native transport links the codec statically. Upstream source is not duplicated here.

The v0.2.0 release includes `Pi2Carplay-v0.2.0-codec-sources.tar.gz` with the exact x264 and libyuv revisions and original BlueZ sbc source archive. Project adapters/build scripts and the complete patched kernel are in the tagged Git source archive. Component notices remain in their respective sources and the image.

x264 commit0480cb05fa188d37ae87e8f4fd8f1aea3711f7ee (GPL); libyuv commit2e65a61dffeb6ab9dd5dd363ccede11770957b73 (BSD/PATENTS). Fetch upstream sources at the exact commits in dependency-revisions.json; upstream archives are not duplicated here. Kernel provenance is recorded in src/kernel/. Our JNI/capture sources and build scripts are in src/capture and scripts. Existing copyright headers and the licenses directory apply.

Android base: AOSP16 Raspberry Pi5, KonstaKANG2026-04-28. Original upstream Android/firmware notices remain in the image. FFmpeg/Raspberry Pi SAND decoder correction and allocator correction sources are supplied separately under src/android/scripts. Proprietary app APKs and the ARM32 protocol SDK are distinct binary components; this repository does not relicense them or claim their source implementation is included. Complete redistribution review is pending before public publication.
